newsitem.title: RUSSIA: After vote, Russia says it averted Belarus crisis.
newsitem.headline: After vote, Russia says it averted Belarus crisis.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin on Monday discussed the results of the controversial referendum in Belarus with his prime minister, Viktor Chernomyrdin, and concluded that Russia's bid to defuse the political crisis in Minsk had worked.

"It was again stressed how timely were the steps Russia took, which allowed a reduction in tension in Belarus society on the eve of the referendum, prevented a social explosion and averted the development of a turn of events for the worse in Russian-Belarussian relations," the Kremlin press service said in a statement.

Chernomyrdin on Friday brokered a compromise between Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko and parliament. But it fell apart within a day and Lukashenko went ahead with the vote on Sunday. The results gave massive backing to his bid for vast new powers.

Chernomyrdin said on Sunday that a group of Belarus legislators were responsible for blocking the compromise, but also expressed irritation with Lukashenko for failing to do enough to make the accord work.

Moscow favors Lukashenko's quest for closer ties with Russia but fears his autocratic style and lack of free-market economic reforms could prove a burden in the two-state union agreed by Yeltsin and the Belarus president last April.

The Kremlin said Chernomyrdin met Yeltsin for an hour and a half at the Barvikha sanatorium near Moscow, where the president is convalescing. It is the longest reported working meeting Yeltsin has had since his heart bypass operation on November 5.
The two men also discussed the new framework peace agreement Chernomyrdin signed on Saturday with the leader of the Chechen separatist government and Moscow's further strategy on the problem.
They also talked about efforts to pay overdue wages to public sector employees and the armed forces.
Yeltsin gave Chernomyrdin instructions for the prime minister's visits to France and Poland this week. He leaves for Paris on Monday evening.
